Class Database

java.lang.Object
Database
public class Database extends Object
All JDBC access lives here. Connection settings come from db.properties (url, user, password) so credentials are not hard-coded or committed. Tables used (from sql/seed.sql): menu_items(id, name, category, price) inventory(inventory_id, name, quantity, unit, restock_threshold) recipe_items(item_id, inventory_id, amount) employees(employee_id, name, role, hourly_rate, active) (see sql/employees.sql) orders(order_id, order_time, employee_id, subtotal, tax, tip, total, payment_method) order_item(order_item_id, order_id, item_id, quantity, price)

    • getHourlySales

      public List<Database.HourlySales> getHourlySales(LocalDate day) throws SQLException
      X-report: orders, sales, tax, tips, and payment totals per hour for one day. Read-only, so it can be run as often as needed. Seed data stores "card"/"cash"/"mobile" while the cashier screen stores "Credit Card"/"Debit Card"/"Cash"/"Gift Card", so payments are grouped into cash, card, and other.
      Parameters:
      day - the day to report on
      Returns:
      one entry per hour that had orders, in hour order
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the query fails

    • submitOrder

      public int submitOrder(List<CartItem> cart, double discount, double tip, String paymentMethod, int employeeId) throws SQLException
      Saves one order and its line items in a single transaction, then subtracts the ingredients each drink uses (recipe_items) from inventory.
      Parameters:
      cart - the drinks in the order
      discount - the dollar amount taken off the subtotal
      tip - the tip amount in dollars
      paymentMethod - how the customer paid, such as Cash or Credit Card
      employeeId - the ID of the cashier who took the order
      Returns:
      the new order's ID
      Throws:
      SQLException - if any part of the order fails to save; nothing is saved in that case
